datasets.title: District-week notifiable infectious disease surveillance, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 2023-2026 (third-party compilation)
datasets.licence_name: CC BY 4.0 (self-declared in the bundled README)
datasets.coverage: 2023 week 16, 2023 weeks 22-52, all 2024, all 2025, 2026 weeks 1-28 (164 of 169 weeks); 59,824 district-week-condition rows
datasets.geography: district / sub-division level within Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province
datasets.indicators: cases (count) for 16 notifiable conditions, no denominator
datasets.notes: IMPORTANT, read before using: the bundled README states this panel was 'transcribed from each bulletin PDF using an AI-assisted document-reading tool' and asks users to 'cite the accompanying Data in Brief article', but names no authors, journal, or DOI anywhere in the supplied files, and a web search for the article by its stated title found no matching publication (only the underlying NIH bulletin PDFs themselves, which are a known, already-used source in this project). The CC BY 4.0 licence claim is therefore self-declared and UNVERIFIED, not confirmed against an independent record, and classified COMPILATION (a derivative re-processing of other documents) rather than SURVEILLANCE for that reason -- permissions() then correctly restricts it to internal validation only regardless of the licence claim. The README's own data-quality section is detailed and candid about known issues (condition right-censoring from 2023 week 32, a district label that changes meaning in 2024 week 50, 26 weeks whose columns do not reconcile to the printed total) -- these are the compiler's own disclosures, not independently verified by this project either. Recommendation: do not treat as a verified source or persist it as observations until you can confirm who produced it and whether the 'Data in Brief article' exists.

datasets.title: Malaria Atlas Project national-unit modelled estimates, Pakistan
datasets.publisher: Malaria Atlas Project (University of Oxford)
datasets.licence_name: CC BY 3.0 (maps); open-access policy states no restriction on publicly sourced data
datasets.geography: country level (admin0), Pakistan only in the supplied file
datasets.indicators: Incidence Rate (cases per thousand, modelled), Infection Prevalence (per 100 children, modelled)
datasets.notes: These are MODELLED ESTIMATES produced by MAP's statistical models (which blend survey data, routine reporting and covariates), not raw case counts or direct surveillance observations -- classified HEALTH_CONTEXT, not SURVEILLANCE, for that reason. Supplied without its generating script, but a copy of the 'malariaAtlas' R package source (the tool MAP publishes for programmatic access to this exact data) was supplied alongside it (malariaAtlas-master.zip), which is consistent with -- though does not prove -- that provenance. Must never be plotted or compared on the same axis as a case-count series (e.g. the NIH bulletin or OpenDengue data above) without clearly labelling one as modelled and the other as reported.

datasets.geography: country level (admin0) for most rows; some countries carry admin1
datasets.indicators: dengue_total (count), case_definition_standardised (Suspected/Confirmed/Total -- not uniform across rows, see notes)
datasets.notes: Published, peer-reviewed compilation (Scientific Data, 2024; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-024-03120-7 -- paper located by search, not independently re-read for its exact licence text from this sandbox). case_definition_standardised varies by row within the same country -- some Pakistan rows are 'Suspected and confirmed', others 'Confirmed', others 'Total'; mixing these without filtering to one definition silently changes what is being measured. T_res also mixes Week/Month/Year within one series; resampling to a common period before use, and never comparing rows of different T_res directly, is required.
